channel.title: Veille IA et cybersécurité — Yuung Kansietoko
channel.description: Articles sur l'intelligence artificielle dans la cybersécurité et failles exploitées liées à l'IA, agrégés toutes les heures depuis The Hacker News, BleepingComputer, Dark Reading, SecurityWeek, Le Monde Informatique, Embrace The Red, Simon Willison, le CERT-FR et la CISA.

item.title: [SecurityWeek] AI Inference Providers Failed to Detect Hacking and Prompt Theft, Says Dragos
item.description: Dragos uncovered undetected intrusions at three AI inference providers using nearly two million prompts sent to AI services. The post AI Inference Providers Failed to Detect Hacking and Prompt Theft, Says Dragos appeared first on SecurityWeek .

item.title: [The Hacker News] AI-Assisted Cyber Attacks Trigger Unauthorized Payments at Indian Banks and Fintech Firms
item.description: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has warned that threat actors are carrying out artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted cyber attacks targeting information and communication technology (ICT) assets in the country. This unsanctioned activity has resulted in unauthorized financial…

item.title: [BleepingComputer] Signal to block Siri, Gemini AI from capturing chats on iOS, Android
item.description: Signal has announced new protections that block screenshots on iOS 27 and prevent AI assistants from capturing conversations on supported Android devices. [...]

item.title: [The Hacker News] OpenRouter Drops 3 Providers After Researchers Catch Months of Prompt Theft at AI Hosting Firms
item.description: Attackers stole data from inside three AI inference providers for months, and none of the three knew until researchers told them, the industrial cybersecurity company Dragos said this week. Some of the stolen requests were flagged as Zero Data Retention, the setting that is supposed to mean a…

item.title: [SecurityWeek] Amazon: China-Linked Hackers’ AI Agents Exploited Medical Software Zero-Day
item.description: A threat actor used autonomous Cairn AI agents to discover and exploit a critical MONAI Label vulnerability. The post Amazon: China-Linked Hackers’ AI Agents Exploited Medical Software Zero-Day appeared first on SecurityWeek .

item.title: [The Hacker News] Attackers' AI Agents Found a Zero-Day in Medical-Imaging Software and Gained Root Access
item.description: Suspected China-linked hackers used autonomous AI agents to find a previously unknown flaw in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging server, and gain root access to a university server, Amazon Threat Intelligence said this week. The flaw allows an attacker with no account to write files…

item.title: [The Hacker News] Signal Blocks AI Agents From Reading Private Chats via Screenshots on Android and iOS
item.description: Signal has announced that it will restrict screenshots by default to stop artificial intelligence (AI) agents from reading private chats on Android and iOS devices, but conceded that the protection is "incomplete." The feature applies to agentic systems built into iOS 27 and on Android versions…

item.title: [Dark Reading] How Security Vendors Are Tackling Access-Control Challenges for AI Agents
item.description: Identity, runtime and development controls are converging as enterprises are tasked with keeping agents within their assigned tasks. But vendors' approaches vary, so CISOs face a choice.

item.title: [BleepingComputer] Bell Canada says 'agentic' hacker stole enterprise customer data
item.description: Bell Canada has confirmed that an "agentic" threat actor breached its systems on November 17, 2026, and stole enterprise customer data, including information from a system used to order and provision telecommunications circuits. [...]

item.title: [Dark Reading] In Security, Words Matter as Much as Tools, Maybe More
item.description: From talking cloud security to using AI, cyber leaders are finding that clear, disciplined communication is now a front-line defense capability across the enterprise.

item.title: [BleepingComputer] Hackers use autonomous AI tool Cairn to find zero-day, take over server
item.description: Threat actors used the open-source AI penetration-testing framework Cairn to find a previously unknown vulnerability in a medical imaging application. [...]

item.title: [Dark Reading] What We Missed: Nvidia CEO Scandal Rocks AI Industry
item.description: In this video, Dark Reading editors discuss some of the news they didn't get a chance to cover, from Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia to Microsoft's recent cloud outage.

item.title: [The Hacker News] Bazuka Android Malware Uses Fake Screen Overlays to Hide Credential Theft and Device Control
item.description: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a previously unknown Android malware framework called Bazuka that offers large language model (LLM) integration for victim management and control at scale. Dutch mobile security company ThreatFabric said it discovered the threat in late October…

item.description: Microsoft announces new AI agent security tools and transparency standards to protect enterprise systems at its Ignite technical conference.

item.title: [The Hacker News] The Path to AI Autonomy in the SOC
item.description: Security leaders are about to hand AI agents a lot more authority. In a recent a16z survey of CISOs at organizations with more than 1,000 employees, 36% said they are comfortable today letting AI agents act autonomously on low-risk security actions. item.title: [The Hacker News] SonicWall Warns Gen 6 Firewalls Won't Get Security Patches, Even for Critical Flaws
item.description: SonicWall has urged all customers still running Generation 6 firewalls to retire and replace them immediately and stop exposing the devices on the internet edge, citing security risks fueled by AI-assisted attacks. "Attackers now use automation and AI to find and exploit unsupported edge devices…

item.title: [Dark Reading] Qwen Incidents Show Self-Hosted AI Models Need Stronger Steering
item.description: Companies deploying AI agents have the illusion of control, but several incidents demonstrate that businesses need to be ready to enforce directions.

item.title: [Dark Reading] Navigating Vulnerability Hysteria in the AI Era
item.description: This installment of the Reporters' Notebook video series examines the fallout from recent high-severity flaw disclosures, exploring how fears of AI-assisted exploits trigger widespread panic, operational disruptions, and growing warning fatigue.

item.title: [The Hacker News] ThreatsDay: GPT-6.2 Jailbreak Flaws, BubbleLoader PNG Malware, $500M Ransom Demands + 17 More Stories
item.description: The easiest way to fool someone is to give them something they already expect. A job offer. A message about a service outage. A familiar app. Nothing looks strange at first. item.title: [Dark Reading] Strike Graph Launches Integration AI to Automate Continuous Compliance Evidence Using Any Existing Tool
item.description: New agentic AI solution leverages APIs to collect compliance evidence from systems and applies it to over 30 frameworks with no duplicate work.

item.title: [Dark Reading] Java4Shell Flaw Threatens Global Enterprises, Java Application Ecosystem
item.description: Discovered using AI, the memory corruption vulnerability affects the OpenJDK runtime and could allow unauthenticated attackers to take over systems.

item.title: [The Hacker News] AI Pentesting Checklist for Web Apps: 15 Questions to Ask Before Choosing a Vendor
item.description: TL;DR Attackers move first. On average, exploitation now starts before a patch exists (Mandiant M-Trends 2026). item.title: [The Hacker News] Quality Isn’t The Main Worry About AI Pentesting — Data Privacy and Production Safety Are
item.description: AI is speeding up how software is built, which means more code, more changes, and more chances for vulnerabilities to reach production. It's speeding up how attackers find and exploit them too, with time-to-exploit now down to a single day. Security testing has to keep up with both. AI pentesting…

item.description: The commercial kit uses attacker-supplied AI models to personalize lures, evade spam filters, and scale campaigns to tens of thousands of targets.

item.description: Malware can lurk inside just 0.00001% of a neural network. How, then, can any user tell it's there?

item.description: The Android malware has expanded from focusing on cryptocurrency theft to full device control, and the attackers have added advanced analysis of stolen information.

Sur les 37 571 applications actives examinées, 35…

item.title: [Dark Reading] Chinese AI Project Scouts Spies in Taiwan Chip Industry
item.description: The CCP built a Big Data system to scrape reams of information and learn about individuals abroad, to potentially target and exploit them. Think Alice Huang Lite.

Ces projets élargissent l’accès aux…

item.title: [Dark Reading] People Are Getting Weird About AI
